thread:
sarah_support: FYI customer reporting 500s + 3-5s p95 latency since ~09:30 UTC. They say requests are being routed to eu-west-1 instead of their pinned us-west-2 region and auth tokens are failing. Escalating. cc @maya_oncall

maya_oncall: Can you paste one or two request_ids and a short repro? Also need the time window and any relevant headers they sent.

sarah_support: Customer provided this example: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"X-Region: us-west-2\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d \"{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}\"`
Response headers they captured: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`, `x-request-id: 01FZ9YQ8X0`, `x-region: eu-west-1`

ben_sre: Looking at infra events -> I see healthcheck flaps for us-west-2 probe pool around 09:28-09:33. Probe agent IPs rotated and several probes failed TTL check. That triggered smart-routing fallback to eu-west-1 for that customer tenant id for ~4m. Logs: `probe/usw2-agent-17 failed check: tcp dial timeout`, `kv-cache health: degraded`

sam_platform: deploy-bot shows a canary roll of healthcheck-agent v1.3.0 at 07:45 UTC yesterday. That release tightened success_threshold from 3 -> 1 for faster failover. Might be too aggressive for noisy probes.

maya_oncall: Aha — lowered threshold would amplify transient probe packet loss into full failover. Can we confirm the config change for that tenant?

ben_sre: Confirmed: tenant routing policy for critical-customers has `failover_threshold: 1` since 07:46. We should bump to 3 and increase weighting to prefer pinned region. Quick mitigation options: 1) patch routing policy to `failover_threshold: 3` 2) rollback agent to v1.2.9 3) temporarily disable cross-region automatic failover for that tenant

sarah_support: Customer impact: auth errors occur because the fallback region uses a different token issuer (short-lived dev tokens). They see billing anomalies from repeated retries as well. They want immediate mitigation + postmortem.

maya_oncall: Can you run these repro steps and share results? 1) set `X-Region: us-west-2` header 2) hit endpoint with the request id header `X-Request-ID: 01FZ9YQ8X0` 3) capture `x-region` in response

ben_sre: Repro snippet (internal):
```
# hit through our lb repro cluster
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"X-Region: us-west-2\" -H \"X-Request-ID: 01FZ9YQ8X0\" https://internal-api.re.redwood/v1/generate
```
Result in my run at 10:05: `x-region: eu-west-1`, `status: 502`, route-changed: `true`

sam_platform: Patching config now. Using internal routing API:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.re.redwood/api/v1/routing/policy/update \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOK\" \ 
  -d '{"tenant_id":"acct_ABC","failover_threshold":3,"prefer_pinned_region":true}'
```
Applied at 10:12 UTC. Also queued rollback of healthcheck-agent to v1.2.9 for canary and will ramp if green.

deploy-bot: rollback job started: healthcheck-agent -> v1.2.9 (canary: agent-17)

ben_sre: After patch, I've seen the tenant route stay in us-west-2 for 10m and no auth mismatches in telemetry. p95 returned to normal. Still need a postmortem on the release change.

maya_oncall: Please keep monitoring for 30m and post the probe logs showing agent-17 behaviour. Sarah, please update the customer: root cause = aggressive healthcheck threshold in new agent release causing false failovers; mitigation = routing policy patched + agent rollback. Offer credit for retries and follow-up postmortem.

sarah_support: Will update customer now. I'll attach the repro steps, our mitigation timeline, and the next steps. Thanks all. :handshake:
